assumptions.medium: liquid water (skin is similar or higher)

dimension_checks.equation: Fresnel normal-incidence transmissivity T_sol = 4 n1 n2 / ((n1+n2)^2 + kappa^2)
dimension_checks.note: standard; correct form for a lossless incident medium

dimension_checks.equation: Beer-Lambert I(z) = I0 exp(-alpha z), alpha = 2 omega kappa / c
Skin depth delta = 1/alpha = c / (2 omega kappa)

dimension_checks.note: standard; inside the target medium n2, not n1, applies

dimension_checks.equation: Induced potential Delta V = P_LF d / (eps0 eps_LF)
Delta V = [2 chi2 T_sol exp(-alpha z) d / (n1 c eps0 eps_LF)] I_peak
I_peak,min >= [n1 c eps0 eps_LF / (2 chi2 T_sol exp(-alpha z) d)] V_th
I_peak,min >= [n1 c eps0 eps_LF (n1+n2)^2 / (8 n1 n2 chi2 d)] exp(2 omega kappa z / c) V_th
dimension_checks.note: consistent; drops the kappa^2 of T_sol (kappa ~ 0.5 for water at 1 THz: ~4% effect)

dimension_checks.equation: 'HWI Standard Equation' I_peak,min >= (1/D) [2 n2 c eps0 eps_LF / (chi2 d)] [((n1+n2)^2 + kappa^2) / (2 omega kappa)] ln(I0/I_target) V_th
dimension_checks.note: INCONSISTENT: the right side has units of intensity x time (J m^-2). ln(I0/I_t)/(2 omega kappa) = z/c, so the exponential depth factor of p. 37 became a linear one; the Fresnel factor also differs from p. 37

dimension_checks.equation: Thermal time tau_th = rho C_p w^2 / (4 k)

evidence_status: SYNTHETIC order-of-magnitude engineering check of Part II's HWI equations with standard reference values. Not a safety assessment; no physical validity of the HWI is claimed or refuted beyond what the stated equations and references imply. Mun Seok Lee has not reviewed or endorsed this analysis.

heating_at_surface.note: T_burst < tau_th (p. 29, p. 38) limits diffusion, not the adiabatic rise within one burst. Because p. 29 scales I_peak by 1/D, the time-averaged intensity D*I_peak does not fall with D.

kBT.note: the paper's 4.11e-21 J corresponds to ~298 K, not 310 K (~4% difference)

p29_vs_p37.note: different units, so no numerical agreement is possible; p. 37 is the consistent form

references.air_breakdown_field: standard dielectric strength of dry air
references.chi2_upper_bound: ZnTe d14 ~ 68.5 pm/V (chi2 = 2 d), one of the strongest THz optical-rectification crystals; a deliberately extreme upper bound. Bulk liquid water is centrosymmetric, so its bulk chi2 vanishes in the electric-dipole approximation (Boyd, Nonlinear Optics, 3rd ed., 2008, sec. 1.5)
references.icnirp_skin_limit_long: ICNIRP 2013 laser guidelines (Health Phys. 105, 271), >1400 nm to 1 mm, >10 s: 10/A_s W m^-2 for 0.01-0.1 m^2 (1000 W m^-2 at 0.01 m^2), 100 W m^-2 above 0.1 m^2
references.membrane_eps_lf: lipid hydrocarbon core ~2 (low value favours the paper)
references.q_gating: Shaker K+ channel ~13 e0: Aggarwal & MacKinnon, Neuron 16, 1169 (1996), doi:10.1016/s0896-6273(00)80143-9; Schoppa et al., Science 255, 1712 (1992)
references.skin_note: In vivo skin is water-dominated at THz and of the same order or higher (Pickwell et al., Phys. Med. Biol. 49, 1595 (2004), doi:10.1088/0031-9155/49/9/001)
references.v_th_depolarisation: rest about -70 mV to threshold about -55 mV (Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science, 6th ed., 2021; cited by Part II)
references.water_alpha_per_cm: Xu, Plaxco & Allen, J. Chem. Phys. 124, 036101 (2006), Table I (https://www.itst.ucsb.edu/~sjallen/Pubs/PubJChemPhys.pdf)
references.water_n_1thz: approx.; Kindt & Schmuttenmaer, J. Phys. Chem. 100, 10373 (1996), doi:10.1021/jp960141g; Thrane et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 240, 330 (1995)

snr_p40_at_V_th.note: dimensionless and plausible (~7) once Delta V = V_th is reached; it says nothing about whether Delta V can be reached
